questions.stem:
A train travels along a straight horizontal track between two stations $A$ and $B$.
The train starts from rest at station $A$ and accelerates uniformly for $T$ seconds until it reaches a speed of $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
The train then travels at a constant speed of $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ for 3 minutes before decelerating uniformly until it comes to rest at station $B$.
The magnitude of the acceleration of the train is twice the magnitude of the deceleration.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) On the axes below, sketch a speed–time graph to illustrate the motion of the train as it moves from station $A$ to station $B$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Correct shape with acceleration steeper than deceleration (ignore entries on the axes).
B1: Correct vertical label.
B1: Correct horizontal labels. Accept use of their T or appropriately labelled delineators.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Stations $A$ and $B$ are 4.8 km apart.
(b) Find the value of $T$
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $T$ and $2T$ seen or implied, for acceleration and deceleration in that order.
M1: A clear attempt to use the total area under the graph (or use suvat formulae) and equate to 4800 (or 4.8) to form an equation in $T$ only or their unknown only (e.g. replace $T$ by $\frac{20}{a}$). Must involve a triangle or a trapezium (M0 if they use a single suvat formula for the whole motion).
A1: An equation with at most one error. (use of 3 instead of 180 is one error). Having $T$ and $2T$ round the wrong way, treat as one error.
A1: A fully correct equation.
A1: $T=40$ (allow t) cao
N.B. If attempting to use a single trapezium, and '180' appears in the bracket i.e. $\frac{1}{2}\times 20('T\ terms'+180)$, allow at least M1A1 for one correct parallel side.
N.B. $\frac{1}{2}\times 20(x+180)=4800 \Rightarrow x=300$ ONLY scores B0M1A1A0A0
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Any of: $4800=\left(\frac{20\times T}{2}\right)+(180\times20)+\left(\frac{20\times2T}{2}\right)$; $4800=\left(\frac{20\times T}{2}\right)+\frac{1}{2}\times20(180+(180+2T))$; $4800=\frac{1}{2}\times20(180+T+180)+\left(\frac{20\times2T}{2}\right)$; $4800=\frac{1}{2}\times20(180+3T+180)$; $4800=20\times(180+3T)-\left(\frac{20\times T}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{20\times2T}{2}\right)$ M1A1A1

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) Find the acceleration of the train during the first $T$ seconds of its motion.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: $20 = a\times \text{their } T$ oe
A1ft: Acceleration $=\frac{1}{2}\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ Correct answer, follow through on their '40'

questions.stem:
A particle $P$ is moving with constant acceleration $(-4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$
At time $t=0$, $P$ has velocity $(14\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Find the speed of $P$ at time $t=2$ seconds.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Velocity $=(14\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})+2(-4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})$
M1: Speed $=\sqrt{6^2+(-3)^2}$ Use of Pythagoras to find the speed when $t=2$ with their velocity.
A1 cso: Speed $=\sqrt{45}=3\sqrt{5}=6.7\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ or better ($6.70820\ldots$). Must come from correct velocity.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Accept the use of column vectors throughout
- M1: Correct use of $t=2$ to find the velocity (unsimplified).

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the size of the angle between the direction of $\mathbf{i}$ and the direction of motion of $P$ at time $t=2$ seconds.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use trig to find an equation in a relevant angle e.g. $(90^\circ-\theta)$ for their velocity, e.g. $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{6}\right)$
A1ft: Correct equation for a relevant angle, ft on their v
A1: $27^\circ$ or better OR $333^\circ$ or better, $0.46$ rads or better OR $5.8$ rads or better. Cao. No isw (A0 for a negative answer)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
At time $t=T$ seconds, $P$ is moving in the direction of vector $(2\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})$
(c) Find the value of $T$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Use of $v=u+aT$ to obtain a velocity vector in $T$ (allow t): $v=(14\mathbf{i}-5\mathbf{j})+(-4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})T$
OR $v=(6\mathbf{i}-3\mathbf{j})+(-4\mathbf{i}+\mathbf{j})t$ ($t=T-2$)
M1: Use ratios, using their velocity, to produce an equation in $T$ only (Allow reciprocal and incorrect sign): $\frac{14-4T}{-5+T}=\frac{2}{-3}$
A1: Correct equation in $T$ only
A1: $T=3.2$ Cao
N.B. If they use their answer to (a) instead of u = (14i − 5j) but never correct their value of t, can score M1M1A0A0
N.B. If they use v = k(2i − 3j) to produce 2 simultaneous equations in k and T, and then they use a calculator to solve and get T=3.2, award all the marks, but if they get the wrong answer, they lose the last 3 marks.

questions.stem:
A branch $AB$, of length 1.5 m, rests horizontally in equilibrium on two supports.
The two supports are at the points $C$ and $D$, where $AC=0.24\,\mathrm{m}$ and $DB=0.36\,\mathrm{m}$, as shown in Figure 1.
When a force of 150 N is applied vertically upwards at $B$, the branch is on the point of tilting about $C$.
When a force of 225 N is applied vertically downwards at $B$, the branch is on the point of tilting about $D$.
The branch is modelled as a non-uniform rod $AB$ of weight $W$ newtons.
The distance from the point $C$ to the centre of mass of the rod is $x$ metres.
Use the model to find
(i) the value of $W$
(ii) the value of $x$

parts.text:
Use the model to find
(i) the value of $W$
(ii) the value of $x$
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: $R_D=0$ for scenario 1 or $R_C=0$ for scenario 2 seen on a diagram or implied by working.
Scenario 1, M(C): $(150\times1.26)=Wx$
M1: Complete method to form an equation in $W$ and a consistent unknown distance only, for scenario 1. All equations used must be dimensionally correct and have the correct no. of terms but condone sign errors. (M0 if $R_D=0$ is never used)
A1: Correct unsimplified equation in $W$ and $x$ or their defined unknown distance.
Scenario 2, M(D): $(225\times0.36)=W(0.9-x)$
M1: Complete method to form an equation in $W$ and a consistent unknown distance only, for scenario 2. All equations used must be dimensionally correct and have the correct no. of terms but condone sign errors. (M0 if $R_C=0$ is never used)
A1: Correct unsimplified equation in $W$ and $x$ or their defined unknown distance
dM1: Dependent on both M's, solve simultaneous equations for either $W$ or their unknown, e.g. $0.81W=243$
A1: Correct answer for $W$: $W=300$
A1: Correct answer for $x$: $x=0.63$ This must be the distance stated in the question, from C to the centre of mass.
N.B. If they include g in a moments equation, they lose the A mark for that equation and both final A marks.
Alternative moments equations (Scenario 1): M(A) $(R_C\times0.24)+(150\times1.5)=W(x+0.24)$; M(G) $R_C x=150(1.26-x)$; M(B) $(R_C\times1.26)=W(1.26-x)$; M(D) $(R_C\times0.9)=(150\times0.36)+W(0.9-x)$; Vert $R_C+150=W$.
Alternative moments equations (Scenario 2): M(A) $(R_D\times1.14)=(225\times1.5)+W(x+0.24)$; M(C) $(225\times1.26)+Wx=(R_D\times0.9)$; M(G) $R_D(0.9-x)=225(1.26-x)$; M(B) $(R_D\times0.36)=W(1.26-x)$; Vert $R_D=225+W$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- N.B. B0 means there are no other marks available.
- Scenario 1: Equations with unknown distance, $x$, measured from C. Complete method will involve one moments equation with $R_D=0$ or two equations with $R_C$ eliminated and $R_D=0$. M0 if $R_D$ never equals zero
- Scenario 2: Equations with unknown distance, $x$, measured from C. Complete method will involve one moments equation with $R_C=0$ or two equations with $R_D$ eliminated and $R_C=0$. M0 if $R_C$ never equals zero

questions.stem:
Three points $P$, $Q$ and $R$ are on a horizontal road where $PQR$ is a straight line.
The point $Q$ is between $P$ and $R$, with $PQ=6x$ metres and $QR=5x$ metres, as shown in Figure 2.
A vehicle moves along the road from $P$ to $Q$ with constant acceleration.
The vehicle is modelled as a particle.
At time $t=0$, the vehicle passes $P$ with speed $u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
At time $t=12$ s, the vehicle passes $Q$ with speed $2u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
Using the model,

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Considers P to Q and forms a relevant equation in terms of $u$ and $x$: $6x=\left(\frac{u+2u}{2}\right)12$ OR $6x=12u+\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{u}{12}\times12^2$ OR $(2u)^2=u^2+2\times\frac{u}{12}\times6x$
A1*: Reaches given answer from correct working, $x=3u$ *

parts.label: b
parts.text:
As the vehicle passes $Q$, the acceleration of the vehicle changes instantaneously to $1.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$
The vehicle continues to move with a constant acceleration of $1.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ and passes $R$ with speed $3u\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$
Using the model,
(b) find the value of $u$,
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
Q to R: M1: e.g. $(3u)^2=(2u)^2+2(1.5)(15u)$
A1: Correct unsimplified equation in $u$ only
A1: $u=9$ Correct answer
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Uses the given answer in (a) to form an equation in u only. N.B. If brackets missing, allow M1, but allow recovery.

parts.label: c
parts.text:
(c) find the distance travelled by the vehicle during the first 14 seconds after passing $P$
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
Q to S (t = 14 position):
M1: Complete method to find the distance travelled in the 2 seconds after passing Q: $QS=2u\times2+\frac{1}{2}\times1.5\times2^2$
A1: Correct unsimplified expression in $u$ only (or 39 m)
M1: Complete method to find the required distance (need $18u$ or $6x$): $(4u+3)+18u$
A1: $201$ (m) Correct answer

questions.stem:
A boat is pulled along a river at a constant speed by two ropes.
The banks of the river are parallel and the boat travels horizontally in a straight line, parallel to the riverbanks.
• The tension in the first rope is 500 N acting at an angle of $40^\circ$ to the direction of motion, as shown in Figure 3.
• The tension in the second rope is $P$ newtons, acting at an angle of $\alpha^\circ$ to the direction of motion, also shown in Figure 3.
• The resistance to motion of the boat as it moves through the water is a constant force of magnitude 900 N
The boat is modelled as a particle. The ropes are modelled as being light and lying in a horizontal plane.
Use the model to find
(i) the value of $\alpha$
(ii) the value of $P$

parts.text:
Use the model to find
(i) the value of $\alpha$
(ii) the value of $P$
(8)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Form an equation perpendicular to the direction of motion. Correct number of terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion: $500\sin40^\circ=P\sin\alpha^\circ$
A1: Correct unsimplified equation.
M1: Form an equation parallel to the direction of motion. If using $F=ma$ then must have $a=0$. Correct number of terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion: $500\cos40^\circ+P\cos\alpha^\circ=900$
A1: Correct unsimplified equation.
(i) M1: Form and solve an equation in $\alpha$: $\tan\alpha^\circ=\frac{500\sin40^\circ}{900-500\cos40^\circ}$
A1: $\alpha=32$ or better ($31.8683\ldots$) (Accept 32 or better as their final answer)
(ii) M1: Form and solve an equation in $P$: $P=\frac{500\sin40^\circ}{\sin31.868\ldots^\circ}$
A1: $P=610$ or better ($608.736\ldots$)
N.B. Penalise over accurate answers only once for the question.
ALTERNATIVE USING A TRIANGLE OF FORCES:
Cosine Rule: $P^2=500^2+900^2-2\times500\times900\cos40^\circ$ OR $500^2=P^2+900^2-2\times P\times900\cos\alpha^\circ$ OR $900^2=P^2+500^2-2\times P\times500\cos(140^\circ-\alpha^\circ)$ (M1A1)
Sine Rule/Lami's Theorem: $\frac{P}{\sin40^\circ}=\frac{500}{\sin\alpha^\circ}=\frac{900}{\sin(140^\circ-\alpha^\circ)}$ (any two) (M1A1)
(i) M1A1: Solve for $\alpha$: $\alpha=32$ or better ($31.8683\ldots$)
(ii) M1A1: Solve for $P$: $P=610$ or better ($608.736\ldots$)
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (i) M1: Form and solve an equation in $\alpha$ (This an M mark so do not penalise accuracy of manipulation)
- (ii) M1: Form and solve an equation in P (This an M mark so do not penalise accuracy of manipulation)
- A1: Accept 32 or better (i.e 32, 31.9, 31.87,… as their final answer)
- A1: Accept 610 or better (i.e 610, 609, 608.7,… as their final answer)
- ALTERNATIVE: M1 Use cosine rule to give an equation in P (and $\alpha$ possibly) A1 Correct equation. M1 Use sine rule to give an equation in P and $\alpha$ A1 Correct equation. N.B. They could use the Sine or the Cosine Rule twice to obtain their two equations.

questions.stem:
A parcel of mass 2 kg is pulled up a rough inclined plane by the action of a constant force.
The force has magnitude 18 N and acts at an angle of $40^\circ$ to the plane.
The line of action of the force lies in a vertical plane containing a line of greatest slope of the inclined plane.
The plane is inclined at an angle of $30^\circ$ to the horizontal, as shown in Figure 5.
The coefficient of friction between the plane and the parcel is 0.3
The parcel is modelled as a particle $P$

parts.label: a
parts.mark_scheme:
Perpendicular to the plane:
M1: $R+18\sin40^\circ=2g\cos30^\circ$
A1: Correct number of terms, forces resolved perp to the plane where appropriate, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion, forces and angles paired up correctly. Correct unsimplified equation.
Equation of motion parallel to the plane:
M1: $18\cos40^\circ-F-2g\sin30^\circ=2a$ (or -2a). Correct number of terms, forces resolved where appropriate, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion, forces and angles paired up correctly.
A1: Correct unsimplified equation with at most one error.
A1: Fully correct unsimplified equation.
B1: $F=0.3R$ Use of $F=0.3R$
dM1: $18\cos40^\circ-0.3(2g\cos30^\circ-18\sin40^\circ)-2g\sin30^\circ=2a$ Eliminate F and R to form an equation in a, dependent on two M's
A1: $a=1.18$ or $1.2\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}})$ cao. Correct value for a. Must be 2 or 3sf

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The points $A$ and $B$ lie on a line of greatest slope of the plane, where $AB=5\,\mathrm{m}$ and $B$ is above $A$. Particle $P$ passes through $A$ with speed $2\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ in the direction $AB$.
(b) Find the speed of $P$ as it passes through $B$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:

A1: $v=3.98$ or $4.0$ or $4\,(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}})$ Cao. Must be positive. Note that a=1.2 leads to v=4.
Official notes (completeness pass):

parts.label: c
parts.text:
The force of 18 N is removed at the instant $P$ passes through $B$. As a result, $P$ comes to rest at the point $C$.
(c) Determine whether $P$ will remain at rest at $C$. You must show all stages of your working clearly.
(4)

A1: $(a)>0$ OR $(a)<0$. Concludes that P will not remain at rest oe. Correct statement from fully correct working.
